newsitem.title: UK: Bank of Scotland up after Laing comment.
newsitem.headline: Bank of Scotland up after Laing comment.

text.p: Shares in Bank of Scotland Plc and Royal Bank of Scotland Plc rose in a firm UK bank sector on Monday as analysts at Credit Lyonnais Laing repeated "buy" recommendations on both stocks, traders said.
Bank of Scotland shares were up 12p at 309 by 1017 GMT while Royal Bank shares were up 7-1/2p at 565.
Analyst Martin Hughes at Laing said the two Scottish banks had been left behind in the sector's recent rise.
"They offer premium growth prospects and are trading on a discount to the rest of the sector," Hughes said.
Other UK banks were also strong, with Barclays Plc up 8p at 10.75 stg after earlier reaching a record 10.79 stg, Lloyds TSB Group Plc up 6p at 449 and National Westminster Bank Plc up 9-1/2p at 758.

This year's gains in bank stocks come despite the sector's outperformance during 1996, with investors continuing to be lured by the promise of a benign economic backdrop of steady growth and low inflation in which bank profits can flourish.
"The sector has gone straight up, market-makers are short and there is not a seller in sight," said Hughes.
